study.title: Coringa / Godavari delta, Andhra Pradesh
study.question: Do surface-water and vegetation signals in the Coringa mangrove creeks differ between seasonally matched 2020 and 2025 observations, and how far can a masked NDVI difference be trusted at this tidal site?
phenomena: surface water extent in tidal creeks
limitations: Tidal stage and turbidity are uncontrolled confounders.

aoi.boundary_source: Manually placed over the mangrove/creek complex of Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary south of Kakinada; not the official sanctuary boundary.

can_conclude: Masked NDVI/NDWI/MNDWI differences between seasonally matched 2020 and 2025 observations on one grid, with the shared-valid footprint stated.
How the candidate-change area responds as the difference threshold tightens (threshold sweep).
How much the estimate moves under single-pair versus composite estimators and leave-one-out resampling for this AOI and grid.
cannot_conclude: Proven mangrove loss or gain, ecological causation, or tidal-stage effects.
Any population-level confidence interval: the uncertainty recorded is resampling variability for this AOI and grid.

attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2020-2026), processed by ESA; L2A products distributed by the Element 84 Earth Search STAC catalogue (AWS Open Data). DEM: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (ESA/DLR) where included. Event context: NDRRMA (2025) and ICIMOD (2026) situation reporting, cited as external literature, not project measurements.

limitations: Tidal stage and turbidity are uncontrolled confounders.
The following indices use 20 m SWIR bands resampled to the 10 m analysis grid and contain no genuine 10 m SWIR detail: mndwi.
Composites are robust within-period summaries of a few observations, not a dense time series; inter-annual change is represented by two period composites only.
Index differences are candidate spectral signals. They are not verified deforestation, wetland loss, construction, glacier damage or any other causal land-cover label.
Cloud, shadow and saturated-pixel exclusion relies on the provider SCL product; terrain shadow is not independently re-derived.
Surface reflectance is the provider L2A product; no independent atmospheric correction is performed.
Areas are planimetric on the documented projected grid; UTM scale distortion at this AOI is small but nonzero.

hypothesis_verdicts.statement: H1 (threshold sensitivity): for every index, candidate-change area decreases monotonically as the absolute threshold tightens from 0.05 to 0.25, and the ranking of the three indices by candidate-change fraction at the primary threshold is preserved across the sweep. Measured by the threshold-response sweep with area-conservation checks.

evidence.monotonicity: enforced by threshold_sweep; the run aborts on violation

hypothesis_verdicts.statement: H2 (composite versus single scene): the 3x3-observation median composite yields a smaller absolute mean delta and a narrower single-pair spread than the nine genuine single-scene pairs, because per-scene observation noise (sun angle, tide, atmosphere) partially averages out. Measured by comparing the composite_median estimator against the single_pairs family.

H3 (temporal robustness): removing any single observation from a composite (leave-one-out) shifts the candidate-change fraction less than the full spread across single-scene pairs. Measured by the leave_one_out family against the single_pairs family at each threshold.

H4 (cross-pipeline consistency): the frozen M0 single-scene NDVI delta and the M1 anchor single-scene NDVI delta agree closely on their shared valid footprint because they use the same two dates and the same formula; residual differences are attributable to mask policy, not processing. Measured by the cross-pipeline comparison on shared pixels.

H5 (validity role): the common-valid footprint is complete for this study, so estimator differences are caused by observation selection, not by validity masks. Measured by the coverage summary and the per-estimator common-valid fractions.

interpretation_guardrails: Candidate-change areas are threshold-dependent descriptions of index difference, not verified environmental change.
For Coringa, an NDVI decrease is not evidence of mangrove loss: tides, seasonality and mixed pixels can produce the same signal.
No independent reference labels were used in this run; no supervised accuracy number is reported anywhere in it.
Estimator differences measure observation-selection effects, not processing errors.
